card.name: Neuropsychiatric symptoms and similar modifiers
card.fires_on: The word right after a descriptive modifier in a medical phrase, mostly "symptoms" after "neuropsychiatric", or "behavioral" in "mental status and behavioral changes". Also fires on "-functional" in "non-functional".

modes.label: Symptoms after neuropsychiatric
modes.description: The word "symptoms" right after "neuropsychiatric" in warnings about stopping or restarting therapy.
modes.example: Consider the risks and benefits for the individual patient to determine if therapy with KALYDECO should be interrupted at the occurrence of neuropsychiatric<< symptoms>>.

modes.label: Modifier before a noun
modes.description: An adjective such as behavioral, beneficial or supportive that sits just before a noun like changes, insects or therapy.
modes.example: patients with Parkinson's disease may experience new or worsening mental status and<< behavioral>> changes

modes.label: Non-functional
modes.description: The word "functional" after "non-" in a software requirements sentence.
modes.example: A BDD story can just as easily describe a non<<-functional>> requirement

card.plain: It lights up on the word that finishes a descriptive label, such as "neuropsychiatric symptoms", just before the noun it describes.
